title: INSERT Statements
description: Add rows to a table with INSERT, including single rows, multiple rows, inserting from a query, and capturing values with the OUTPUT clause.

data.text: INSERT adds new rows to a table. It looks simple, but there are several forms — single-row, multi-row, from a query, and with identity override. This lesson covers all of them.

data.title: Insert a single row

data.text: After the INSERT, SQL Server reports the number of affected rows: '(1 row(s) affected)'.

data.title: Omitting columns
data.text: If you omit a column from the INSERT list, SQL Server fills it with: the next IDENTITY value, the DEFAULT value, NULL (if nullable), or a computed value. If none of these apply and the column is NOT NULL, the INSERT fails.

data.title: Multi-row VALUES
data.code:
INSERT INTO sales.promotions (
    promotion_name, discount, start_date, expired_date
)
VALUES
    ('2018 Summer Promotion', 0.15, '20180601', '20180901'),
    ('2018 Fall Promotion',   0.15, '20181001', '20181101'),
    ('2018 Winter Promotion', 0.20, '20181201', '20190101');

data.title: Performance: multi-row is faster
data.text: Inserting 1,000 rows with a single multi-row VALUES statement is dramatically faster than 1,000 individual INSERT statements, because SQL Server parses and plans the query only once.
INSERT ... SELECT — copying data between tables
You can populate a table using the results of a query. This is common for archiving, staging, or ETL (extract, transform, load) workflows.

data.title: Insert results of a query
data.code:
INSERT INTO sales.product_archive (product_id, product_name, archived_at)
SELECT product_id, product_name, GETDATE()
FROM   production.products
WHERE  list_price < 50;

data.text: The OUTPUT clause returns data from the rows that were just inserted — including IDENTITY values that were auto-generated. The 'inserted' pseudo-table holds the new row values.

data.title: Return the generated identity value
OUTPUT into a table variable
data.text: For batch inserts, you can redirect OUTPUT into a table variable or temp table: OUTPUT inserted.id INTO @NewIDs. This is the cleanest way to retrieve hundreds of generated identity values at once.
If a column has the IDENTITY property, SQL Server auto-generates values. To insert your own explicit value (common during data migration), you must enable IDENTITY_INSERT first:

data.title: Override identity with IDENTITY_INSERT
Only one IDENTITY_INSERT per table
data.text: You can only have IDENTITY_INSERT ON for one table (per session) at a time, and only if no other connection is inserting. Remember to turn it OFF when done — it does not reset automatically.

data.title: INSERT at a glance
points: INSERT INTO table (columns) VALUES (values) adds one row
VALUES (row1), (row2), ... inserts multiple rows in one statement
INSERT ... SELECT copies rows from a query into a table
OUTPUT returns the inserted values — use the 'inserted' pseudo-table
SET IDENTITY_INSERT ON lets you provide your own identity values for migration
